- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward by 1–2% to align with true decline.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in subsequent periods; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if price is trending sharply upward, forecast often fails to sustain momentum; adjust downward slightly in next 2–3 periods.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from bullish to bearish) is often not reflected in model; if sentiment drops below 0.33, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate true volatility; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67).
